subject: Habitat Labs — renewal discussion: capacity, term, and pricing
messages:
From: Claire Deng <claire@habitatlabs.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning + Q3 usage and latency notes

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the QBR last week. I wanted to share the Q3 export and a couple of operational notes ahead of our renewal window (Feb 2027). High-level items: 

- Token spend: month-over-month up ~42% for the past three months; last month was 2.1B tokens (mostly embedding-heavy workloads).
- Latency: we saw a recurring tail at 600-900ms for inference that used to sit at ~320-420ms — attached is a latency_trend_nov.png showing the two outage-adjacent spikes.
- Burst usage: during marketing campaigns we hit burst demands ~3x baseline for a 2-3 hour window twice this quarter; burst credits applied but we want a more predictable approach.

We'd like to review options: committed tiers, multi-year term pricing, and a guaranteed burst/override path (so our product team isn't impacted by throttling). Procurement will want an SOW and a straightforward list of tiers/discounts to evaluate. 

Attaching: Q3_Usage_Export.csv and the latency screenshot. Can you and your team propose a few commit tiers and an operational playbook? Also cc'ing Tom (Head of Infra) and procurement.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Deng
Head of Platform
Habitat Labs

---
Attachments: Q3_Usage_Export.csv (csv), latency_trend_nov.png (image)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Deng <claire@habitatlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + Q3 usage and latency notes

Hi Claire — thanks for the artifacts and the clear ask. Quick read-through and initial thoughts below; I'll loop in pricing and your AE for a formal proposal.

Summary observations (from the CSV):
- Baseline monthly tokens: ~1.5B over the last 6 months, with 2.1B last month due to the campaign spike.
- Token mix: ~68% embedding calls, 25% short-generation, 7% long-form generation — matches your product profile.
- Cost impact: your on-demand spend increased ~38% QoQ; a committed tier with batching and caching recommendations should recover ~15–25% of that.

Operational suggestions (quick):
- Commit tiers: propose 1.5B/month (current baseline), 2.5B/month (comfort for campaign headroom), and a 3.5B/month reserved tier with burst credits for short spikes.
- Burst clause: add a short-window burst pool (3x baseline for up to 3 hours, up to 6 times/month) available as paid or as part of a higher-tier commitment.
- Latency work: looks like a warm-start artifact during heavy KV-cache churn — our ops team can run a focused jitter test + kernel tuning during your low-traffic window to flatten the tail.

Next steps: Marissa (CS lead) and Karthik (AE) — can you weigh in on pricing bands and a multi-year discount schedule? Claire, would you prefer a 12- or 24-month term? Procurement contact details would help us draft a simple SOW and a PDF proposal.

Cheers,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Growth
Redwood Inference

---
Related: https://redwood.app/dashboards/habitat/overview
From: Claire Deng <claire@habitatlabs.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@habitatlabs.com>, Procurement <procurement@habitatlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + Q3 usage and latency notes

Sean/Marissa/Karthik — thanks for the quick reply. Preference is a 24-month term if we can get predictable unit economics and burst guarantees. Procurement is asking for:

1) A clear price table for the three tiers you proposed (monthly token commitment, overage rate, and burst window rules).
2) A simple SOW that states service levels (target P50/P95 latency for our primary embedding route), incident response SLA, and audit log retention (we need 12 months).
3) A draft contract with optional addendum for on-prem connector testing (we may run a pilot in Q3 2027).

Tom — feel free to chime in on the latency expectations. Procurement: I'll start an intake ticket with our standard CLA and will share any contract redlines.

Cheers,
Claire
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Habitat renewal — pricing bands and AR options

Looping internal notes into thread (for Sean to share):

- Recommended price bands (net of standard PLG credits):
  * Tier A (baseline): 1.5B/mo — $0.00065/token equivalent effective rate; 12-month min, standard support.
  * Tier B (comfort): 2.5B/mo — $0.00058/token; 24-month term incl. 2 burst windows/month (up to 2x baseline for 3 hours).
  * Tier C (enterprise reserve): 3.5B/mo — $0.00052/token; 24-month term, 6 burst windows/month (up to 3x baseline for 3 hours), extended SLA (24x7), dedicated onboarding credits.

- Overage pricing: pro-rated per 100M tokens at Tier A rate; or convert to next tier for remainder of term if sustained.
- Contract notes: accept 12-month as default but offer a 6% additional net discount for 24-month firm commitment plus 30-day exit with 3x notice on tier downgrade.
- Operational offer: nights/weekend ops window where we can run kernel/tuning work to flatten latency — propose a scheduled maintenance SLO to avoid surprise impact.

Karthik: can you draft a short PDF with the table above and a brief SOW bullet list? I'll add the suggested discount language and SLA bullets.

- Marissa
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Deng <claire@habitatlabs.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@habitatlabs.com>, Procurement <procurement@habitatlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Habitat Labs — draft proposal and next steps

Claire/Tom/Procurement team — attaching a short draft proposal that captures the three commit tiers, proposed 24-month incentives, burst rules, and the SOW bullets Claire requested. Highlights:

- We recommend Tier B (2.5B/mo) for predictable runway during marketing campaigns with the 24-month discount (6% off list).
- Included: 6 burst windows/month at 2x baseline for up to 3 hours (this is in the draft as an optional add-on, can be included in Tier C).
- Ops plan: Redwood ops will perform a targeted cache warm-up and kernel tuning during a 2-hour maintenance window agreed with Tom to reduce P95 tail.
- Next steps: if this looks good, procurement can confirm contact details and we'll produce a final contract + DocuSign link; otherwise we can iterate on tier sizes or discount.

Attaching: draft-proposal-Habitat-2027-2028.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-minute call this week to finalize.

Best,
Sean
Head of Growth
Redwood Inference
